batch_observations: TEN PLAYS, and the batch splits cleanly: four rest on real measurement, one is genuinely new with a fitted headline, five are outcome-credited. THE HEADLINE DEFECT IS magnitude.terminal_impact_coefficient_carry, because it is the record that LOOKS most rigorous. It declares D24 state (a) verbatim - 'CORPUS SEARCHED, INSTANCES FOUND' - names a base rate, names one counterexample and refuses to explain it away, and measures a net-vs-range corollary. I reproduced its arithmetic exactly from the committed evidence files (k3 = |ph3 pxchg| / |ph3 sflow| gives 0710 0.3021, 0713 0.0258, 0714 0.0177 = the record's '0.302 -> 0.026 -> 0.018'; 0703's ph3 flow is -489 against the stated 500 floor = the record's own declared boundary weakness). Applying the play's own bar to G20 and G23 reproduces n=6 and 5/6 at <=$200 to the day. But the identical evidence exists for all SEVEN blocks G17-G23, and the search stopped at two. Extended: 12 numb seams, 5/12 at <=$200 against a 24% base rate - and the five hits are ALL in G20+G23 while the six seams in G17/G18/G19 are 0-for-6 (next-day |net| 380/420/1230/720/360/420). The effect is exactly co-extensive with the blocks that were searched. The range corollary also fails to extend (median next-day range 1,205 after a numb seam vs 1,140 otherwise - no compression, where the record measured 1.5x). A CORPUS SEARCH ASSERTED AT 2-OF-7 SCOPE IS THE D24 DISCIPLINE PERFORMED AS A LABEL. THE SECOND STRUCTURAL FINDING is daytype.friday_exit_decomposition, the play the whole Friday->Monday cascade doctrine stands on. Its product is an OPEN-TIME exit LABEL. On the eight weekend-feeding Fridays of G20-G23 the refine CHANGED the blind's label on SIX; only 0605 and 0703 survived the price reveal. Three of the eight refine labels are outside the four canonical types altogether, each declared as new in so many words ('a fifth type, not one of the four'; 'not any of the four labels the blind ruled out'; 'a THIRD exit form'). A four-type taxonomy that does not span its own scope, emitted at a 2-of-8 survival rate, is not an open-time product. THE RECURRING MICRO-DEFECT, in three separate plays: a MAGNITUDE or SHAPE play credited on DIRECTION. shape.grind_vs_spike declares 'scope: leg side + hold-vs-fade (intraday); NOT the day net' and is then FORWARD-CONFIRMED on G11 because 'both sides HIT' on day nets (0119 guessed +1600 against +550). magnitude.catalyst_condition_sort raises its confidence 0.45 -> 0.5 on the same 0119 because it 'earned the side'. magnitude.shoulder_weather_band_void calls G15 0319/0322 correct applications on sign while the void down-size ran 35% and 365% under on the quantity it targets. THE HONEST GAPS RUN THE OTHER WAY TOO: daytype.covering_giveback_self_limiting is UNDER-recorded, not over-credited - its brain record stops at G18 while G21 carries BOTH limbs of the mechanism in one block (the 06-09 COT at WoW -7,763 and 1-yr pctile 2.83 armed 0615, which delivered +910 with absorb_session TRUE and ph3 -1,451 absorbed under +520; the SAME report at age 6.35 days was declared spent and 0619 delivered -110), and G22 0626 and G23 0710 add two more clean declines. And monday.overnight_headfake_into_catchup still carries 'forward_evidence: NONE - G17+ is the forward test' after seven blocks of G17+ have run; I ran it, and it passes (gap sign matches the regular-session net on 5/14 Mondays = 36%, while the inherited D-1 tilt matches on 8/13 = 62%). CONDITION HEALTH, measured on the served state, is the other systematic finding. Three of the batch's numeric bars are degenerate: the near-window HDD <=13.5 bar fires 0/12 in G11/G12/G13 and 10/10 in every one of G18-G23, splitting only in G14/G15/G16 (the shoulder blocks it is named for); the companion 16.4 bar is degenerate in 9 of 12 blocks; and monday.overnight_headfake's parsed condition points at tape_conditions.session_b_share, the known-biased single-sided series, whose <0.50 bar is satisfied on 100% of days in five of the eight blocks where it is served (the two-sided series splits 5/10 in every served block, and B's own 0629 posterior corrected for this by hand). SEVEN OF TEN PLAYS CARRY AN EMPTY falsifier FIELD; I proposed one for each. ONE RECORD DEFECT: daytype.covering_giveback_self_limiting's confidence slot holds PROSE where every other play holds a float, so that play has no numeric confidence at all.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM: a front-loaded capture means the move is already paid for and round-trips; a slow build is continuous repricing that holds. SUPPORT: a per-leg rate on the committed fingerprint store, and I reproduced it independently. Across all 108 days / 6,358 legs in renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json, legs with peaked_fast=true (time-to-peak <= 60s) fail to hold (retention < 0.5 at the 1800s horizon) on 1,234 of 1,246 = 99.0%; only 12 held. On the 6 pivotal days the brain names, 39 of 40 peaked_fast legs faded (the brain's '23/24' is a narrower subset of the same set). The relationship is MONOTONE across four time-to-peak buckets: hold rate 1.0% (0-60s) -> 5.8% (60-300s) -> 16.1% (300-900s) -> 59.2% (900-1800s). TWO QUALIFICATIONS THE RECORD DOES NOT MAKE. (a) The two limbs are not symmetric: the SPIKE-FADES limb is near-deterministic, but the GRIND-HOLDS limb is a minority outcome - non-peaked_fast legs hold only 1,915 of 5,112 = 37.5% pooled, and reach 59% only in the slowest bucket. 'A slow GRIND holds (ride)' overstates its own evidence. (b) Retention is measured at a fixed 1800s horizon, so a peak at 60s has 1,740s to decay while a peak at 1,700s has 100s; part of the gradient is definitional. The monotone ordering survives that, the 1%-vs-59% headline does not fully. THE CONTRADICTION: the play's scope says 'leg side + hold-vs-fade (intraday); NOT the day net', yet its G11 FORWARD-CONFIRMED line reads 'both sides HIT' on two DAY NETS - a quantity the play excludes by its own words, on a day it oversized 2.9x.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, emphatically, and this is the strongest single measurement in the batch. The hold rate could have been flat across the four time-to-peak buckets, or inverted, or the 12 spike-legs that held could have been 400. It is monotone across 6,358 legs on 108 days, and I computed it from the raw fingerprint store rather than reading the claim. The G11 arm is the exception: 'both sides hit' on 2 day nets could not have falsified a leg-level shape claim in either direction, and it is credited to the play anyway.

audits.the_argument: The play sorts expected magnitude by day-condition: UP-size weekend-gap Monday, storage Thursday and swing-reversal/seam; DOWN-size thin-holiday and non-catalyst chop. The entire support is a CURATED LIST OF DAY NETS on the conditions the play names ('Mon: 1020 +2770, 0929 +1240...; Thu: 0918 -1560, 1002 +1360...'), against a shorter list of small non-catalyst days. There is no counted base rate anywhere in the record. I computed one from the actuals: across G17-G23 (70 scored days, 14 storage Thursdays, 14 Mondays), a storage Thursday exceeds its OWN block's median |day_move| on 8 of 14 = 57%, and a Monday on 8 of 14 = 57%. Thursday's MEAN |move| is 850 against 435-526 for the other day-classes, so the TAIL claim survives - but that mean is carried by two days (0528 +2100, 0709 -2050), and this desk's standing rule forbids leading with a mean. In the CDD block G22 the two storage Thursdays (0625 -60, 0702 0) were the two SMALLEST days of the block against a 575 median, a direct contradiction of the flagship up-size arm. The calibration history is a WIDENING TENT: every time an extreme cleared the band top, the response was a new band (s97_2 winter bands, s98_2 year-end amplifier) and never a falsification - the record's own forward line says 'FORWARD-FAILED in calibration on every block' and keeps the play. And the G11 note raises confidence 0.45 -> 0.5 because the play 'earned the SIDE' on 0119 - a DIRECTION result banked by a play whose declared target is magnitude, on a day it oversized 3x.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: MOSTLY NO. The exemplar lists are selected on the outcome they exist to explain; a big day on a catalyst condition is entered as evidence and a small one is not counted. Two things DID come out the other way and are honestly recorded - the G7 1111 Veterans Day refutation of the thin-holiday down-size (15x under, re-scoped to require no live weather catalyst) and the standing 'the band tops are low' admission. Those are real. But the core up-size claim has never been scored against a base rate, and when I score it, it is 57% - four points better than a coin flip on the split it implies.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES, and this is NOT the play's problem. The trigger is a categorical day-class sort, so it splits every block by construction - each 10-day block carries two storage Thursdays, two Mondays and roughly four non-catalyst sessions. The problem is DISCRIMINATION, not state change: measured against each block's own median |day_move| across G17-G23, storage Thursdays land above on 8/14 and Mondays on 8/14 (both 57%), against Wednesdays 6/14 and Fridays 5/14. The sort is real in the TAIL (Thursday mean |move| 850 vs 435-526) and near-null at the median. That is exactly the D23 distinction: the form is fine, the RATE is close to uninformative.
audits.falsifier: The brain's falsifier field is EMPTY, which for a play at confidence 0.5 carrying nine years of accumulated band revisions is the finding. Proposed: over >= 3 unseen blocks, storage Thursdays and weekend-gap Mondays fail to exceed their own block's median |day_move| more often than the non-catalyst sessions do. Second, and it should be stated as policy: a band top exceeded by an extreme counts as a MISS, not as a request for a new band.

audits.the_argument: A five-arm rhythm class (B1 crashes arrive single; B2 bounces run 1-2 days never 3; B3 bounce-death gives a full crash band; B4 in-chain confirming prints size down; B5 more small days), each arm supported by a curated list of day-pairs that fit it. n = 2 blocks in ONE winter. The falsification history is the whole story: the record says 'FORWARD-FAILED on G11' - B2 broke on 0119/0120/0121, which ran three days and ACCELERATED - and then RETAINS B2 with a boundary condition invented after the fact that exactly excludes the breaking instance ('it applies only while no C1 band-break has printed'). The s101_3 block then records a SECOND 3-day counter-run against a B2 call (0203-0205) and re-scopes B2 a second time ('B2 owns BLEED-RHYTHM bounces'; the rest becomes a new FED-RECOVERY band). Two refutations, two post-hoc narrowings, zero retirements. The one full-block forward test scored 6/12 direction with the BLOCK LEAN WRONG - the record's own note says 'the bleed frame carried a down polarity through a block whose intraday nets summed +12,690'. And the caveats concede the structural hole: 'the class has no exit condition - it was carried intact through a block that reversed'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: THE ARM LISTS, NO - crashes_single, bounces_1_2_days, bounce_death_crash and small_day_prevalence are enumerations of the day-pairs that fit, drawn from the two blocks the class was written on. THE FORWARD TESTS, YES, AND THEY CAME OUT AGAINST IT TWICE - and both times the answer was a new boundary condition rather than a retirement or a scoped refutation. A rule that has never been allowed to fail is not a rule that has been tested.

audits.condition_can_change_state: IN PRINCIPLE YES (a parabolic termination without a birth driver is a real, observable configuration), IN PRACTICE NOT FOR SEVEN BLOCKS. I found it stood down in every modern posterior that names it - G22 0626, G23 0707, and the G23 state audit lists it only as a play AFFECTED by the consensus-store hole, not as one that fired. Its two applications are G10 (confirmed) and G11 (block lean wrong). A class that cannot fire for seven consecutive blocks and has no exit condition when it does fire is carrying a live risk of being carried through the next reversal exactly as it was through G11.
audits.falsifier: The brain's falsifier field is EMPTY, which is why two refutations could be absorbed as scoping. Proposed, and it has to be pre-registered: name the bleed class BEFORE a block opens; the class is refuted if that block's realized cum ends at the OPPOSITE polarity, or if a third-day bounce prints with no prior C1 band-break. The second clause matters because the existing B2 escape hatch was written after the escape.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM, ARGUED AND PHYSICAL: 'below the baseload floor there is no near-window Bcf mass for a ramp to deliver', so when near-window (D0..D+3) max forecast gw-HDD is under ~13.5 the weather DELIVERY band has no authority and the day reverts to its residual co-condition class one rung down. The form is declared a STEP not a ratio, and both smooth alternatives were measured and rejected (vol-scaling breaks G12 0203 at 3.3x; a headroom ratio leaves 0305 out) - that is a real functional-form comparison. There is a genuine NEGATIVE CONTROL and I verified it: every winter delivery-band day clears the gate. Computed off the served state, near-window max forecast gw-HDD is above the void bar on 12/12 days in each of G11, G12 and G13. BUT THE HEADLINE POSITIVE NUMBER IS FITTED. The evidence line reads '0305: near-window 13.4 max, call +550 vs actual +470' - and that +550 is the G14 REFINE-v2 number, produced on the block the play was derived from with the actual in hand; that pass ran 12/12 with every single day inside ~200 of actual. The G14 BLIND had 0305 at -900 against +470. The genuine forward instances are G15's 0319 and 0322, and there the record credits SIGN on a play whose target is MAGNITUDE: 0319 -800 vs -1080 (35% under) and 0322 -200 vs -930 (4.6x under). The one recorded mis-application, 0318 at -400 against +1900, was answered with a scoping caveat and 'Confidence unchanged - the gate is sound'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: SPLIT. The winter negative control could have failed and did not - that is a real out-of-sample check across three blocks and I reproduced it. The functional-form rejection is a real comparison. The FOUNDING INSTANCE could not have come out otherwise: it was produced by a refine pass that fit every day of the block to within ~200. So the play has a tested boundary and an untested centre.

audits.falsifier: The brain's falsifier field is EMPTY. audits.the_argument: The play decomposes a Friday close into one of four exit types and has the weekend consume the TYPE rather than the day-net. Its own data_gap field is the confession: 'last-hour signed flow (field #3, the covering/exhaustion tell) is MBO-measured only for G15; for the rest of the record exit-type was inferred from archetype+curve-dir+calendar.' Inferring a type from the archetype - which is written after the Monday is known - is the S108 signature exactly: the label is fitted to the outcome and then the mechanism is credited. The evidence line ('POSITIONING_SPENT: 0327...; ROLL-CARRY: 0206 -> 0209...; FUNDAMENTAL_CARRY: 1128 -> 1201...') is a list of pairs that fit, one per type. I MADE TWO MEASUREMENTS THE RECORD NEVER DID, using the committed exit_states now available for G20-G23. (1) THE LABEL DOES NOT SURVIVE THE PRICE REVEAL. On the eight weekend-feeding Fridays of G20-G23 the refine CHANGED the blind's exit_type on SIX: 0529 (positioning_loaded_carry -> FLOWLESS_BID_WITHDRAWAL -> PASSIVE_LADDER_DISPLACEMENT, renamed twice), 0612 (POSITIONING_SPENT_FADE -> MOMENTUM_CARRY), 0619 (POSITIONING_CARRY -> MOMENTUM_CARRY, 'a correction of my own blind label'), 0626 (MOMENTUM_CARRY -> POSITIONING_SPENT_FADE), 0710 and 0717. Only 0605 and 0703 survived. (2) THE FOUR TYPES DO NOT SPAN THE SPACE. Three of the eight refine labels are outside the taxonomy entirely and the specialist says so each time: 'a fifth type, not one of the four in daytype.friday_exit_decomposition'; 'not any of the four labels the blind ruled out'; 'a THIRD exit form, not either of the two my lens file names'. Across all day-classes in G20-G23 the handoff_out record carries at least eleven distinct non-canonical labels from three specialists.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO for the record's own evidence - a type inferred from archetype+curve-dir after the fact cannot fail, because the archetype is itself written from the outcome. YES for the two measurements I ran, and they came out against the play: 2-of-8 blind label survival and 3-of-8 labels outside the taxonomy are both results that could have come out 8-of-8 and 0-of-8. The play's structural fix - 'Monday inherits the MEASURED exit-state, never the Friday label' - is sound doctrine, but the thing actually emitted at the open is a label, and the label is not stable.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM: a thin overnight book can print a gap on flow that does not confirm it; that gap is a head-fake, and the 06-10 ET catch-up window is where the inherited D-1 tilt reasserts. The call is a pure DIRECTION GATE - 'do NOT inherit the overnight gap sign' - and it sizes nothing. The founding n=2 is MBO-measured and I reproduced it to the digit off the committed evidence: 0316 has high_exc +490 with turn_down at 02:21, phase-0 signed flow -493 against a +230 price move, then phase-1 pxchg -930; 0323 has high_exc +1270, turn at 03:52, phase-0 sflow -26 against +1140, then phase-1 -1920. Those are exactly the record's numbers, and the flow tell is a quantity independent of the day net - it is not the outcome restated. THE FORWARD TEST THE RECORD STILL CALLS PENDING HAS NOW RUN AND IT PASSES. The brain says 'forward_evidence: NONE - proposed S104; G17+ is the forward test', and G17 through G23 have all been walked without anyone scoring it. Measured across those seven blocks: on the 14 Mondays with a non-zero overnight gap, the gap sign matches the regular-session net sign on only 5 = 36%; on the same Mondays the inherited D-1 (prior session) net sign matches on 8 of 13 = 62%. The play's exact claim - drop the gap sign, keep the inherited bias - wins the head-to-head 62% to 36%.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, on both halves. The founding instances could have shown ph0 flow CONFIRMING the gap and the gap holding; they show the opposite twice with the reversal magnitudes recorded. The forward test could have come out at 64% for the gap sign instead of 36%. HONEST LIMIT, which the record should carry: n=14 and p(<=5 of 14 same | fair coin) = 0.21, so the gap-sign result alone is not significant in isolation; the 62%-vs-36% separation on the same Mondays is the stronger read, and it is still n=13.

That makes a directional prediction that can fail, and the discriminator is a served, continuously-varying quantity (COT WoW) read across the specialist's own handoff seam. ORIGIN: G17 0417 fired covering-UP correctly (+40 actual); the blind then RE-FIRED it on 0424 (+250 guess against -380 actual) and the test-drive reverted 0424 to DOWN while leaving 0417 intact. THE RECORD UNDERSTATES ITSELF - it stops at G18, and I found three more clean resolutions. G18 0508 is the cleanest single instance because grp18_blind_E.json carries it as a STRUCTURED rule record with inputs, thresholds, scope_pass and a magnitude band: cot_chg_wow +3,329 (not worsening) -> re-fire declined -> band [-700,-150] -> actual -360, in band and right sign, in the BLIND. G21 carries BOTH LIMBS IN ONE BLOCK: the 06-09 COT printed MM -122,617, WoW -7,763, 1-year percentile 2.83 - a fresh worsening extreme - inside E's 0612 session, and 0615 delivered +910 with absorb_session TRUE and ph3 -1,451 absorbed under +520, which is textbook covering; the SAME report at age 6.35 days on 0619 was declared spent fuel and not re-fired, and 0619 delivered -110. THE WEAKNESS I MUST NAME: the DECLINE branch resolves to 'the chain/state default', so when the play stands down it makes no independent claim and a wrong decline is charged to the chain rather than to this play. audits.the_argument: MECHANISM: where a session CLOSED in its range is a statement about who is holding inventory at the bell, whereas a declining final-phase signed-flow COUNT can equally mean a handover - so take the continuation verdict from close LOCATION, not from flow-shape decay. The brain's own G20 0529 measurement is the sharpening: ph3 was the session's LARGEST phase by volume by 18% (60,930 lots) on a net of only -59, so the prose 'the covering bid went home' described participation and participation was maximal - hence the (VOLUME, NET) pair refinement, objected by B, conceded by E, verified independently by A. THE FOUNDING n=2 REPRODUCES on committed evidence: 0514 close_off_low ~0.86 with phase sflow 118 -> 913 -> 41 (the exact '913 -> 41 decay' the record names) and the next session +320; 0515 close_off_low ~0.76 and Monday 0518 +660. Both closed high on decaying flow and both continued. I THEN RAN THE FORWARD TEST THE RECORD ONLY PROMISES ('rides G20+ Fridays'), off the committed exit_states: on the seven weekend-feeding Fridays of G20-G23, sign(close_off_low_frac - 0.5) predicts the next session's net on 5 of 7; on the tighter >=0.70 / <=0.30 bar it is 4 of 5. THE HEAD-TO-HEAD THE PLAY ACTUALLY ASSERTS COMES OUT ITS WAY: on those same seven Fridays, last-hour SIGNED-FLOW sign predicts 2 of 7 and last-hour PRICE direction 3 of 7. And it is properly a PER-CELL result: pooled over all 40 days carrying exit_states the same bar is 13 of 25 = 52%, a coin flip. The edge lives in the Friday cell, which is the play's declared scope.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, and this is the only play in the batch whose central claim is a HEAD-TO-HEAD against a named alternative on the same days. The comparator (flow shape) could have beaten close location and did not - 2/7 against 5/7 on the identical seven Fridays. The pooled-vs-Friday contrast (52% vs 71-80%) could also have come out the other way, showing a general effect that the Friday scope was needlessly narrowing; instead it confirms the scope. HONEST LIMIT: n = 5 to 7. p(4+ of 5 | fair coin) = 0.19, so no single one of these is significant alone; the pattern across three comparators on the same days is what carries it.

audits.the_argument: This is a META-RULE about how other plays' limbs evaluate, and it is a genuine conditional rule with a trigger, a read and a call, so it is a play and not a descriptor. MECHANISM: an unreachable absolute bar must return UNKNOWN, never a satisfied/refuted boolean - and the specific harm named is that a '<=' bar and a '>=' bar on the SAME unreachable quantity both degrade in the SAME direction (one voids the weather band, the other silently defaults a selector bearish), so several nominally independent artifacts are one artifact wearing several hats. I VERIFIED BOTH BARS IT NAMES BY ID, independently, off the served state. selector.divergence_resolution's gw_hdd >= 16.4: fires 12/12 in G11, 12/12 in G12, then 0/11 in G16 and 0/10 in each of G18, G19, G20, G21, G22, G23 - degenerate in 9 of the 12 blocks with served weather, splitting only G13 (9/12), G14 (4/12) and G15 (3/12). magnitude.shoulder_weather_band_void's near-window <= 13.5: 0/12 in G11, G12 and G13, then 10/10 in every one of G18 through G23 - also degenerate in 9 of 12, splitting only G14, G15 and G16. So the claim 'four independent HDD-keyed artifacts all degraded bearish-or-void in one CDD block' is measurably true on the two bars it names. ITS FALSIFIER IS STATED AND IT SURVIVES: in G11 and G12 the regime is HDD-dominant (D0 gw_hdd 20-41 against gw_cdd 0.0-0.9), so the play is inert there exactly as it claims it must be.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES. Either bar could have split its blocks and neither does - 12/12 and 0/10 are the two ways a threshold can be dead, and both bars produce both, in opposite seasons. This is a rate measurement across twelve blocks, not an exemplar list, and it is reproducible from committed state in one pass. The one thing the record leans on that I would not count is the signed-error attribution ('the blind's four down-calls-that-printed-up contributed -3,840 of a -1,815 drift') - that is an outcome decomposition and it could not have falsified the mechanism.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM, GENUINELY ARGUED: a void is price discovering where liquidity sits; once found, flow stops moving price, so a numb terminal phase (k3 = |ph3 price change| / |ph3 signed flow| <= 0.05 on >= 500 lots) carries into the next session's NET but not into its RANGE. The record is the most disciplined-LOOKING in the batch - it declares D24 state (a) verbatim, names a base rate, names one counterexample and refuses to explain it away, flags its own boundary instance at 489 lots against a 500 floor, and measures the net-vs-range corollary separately. I REPRODUCED ITS ARITHMETIC EXACTLY off renders/ng_refine_s95/g23_mbo_evidence.json: 0710 k3 = 0.3021, 0713 = 0.0258, 0714 = 0.0177, which is the record's '0.302 -> 0.026 -> 0.018'; 0703's ph3 flow is -489, which is the declared 2% boundary miss. Applying the play's own bar to G20 and G23 reproduces n=6 and 5/6 at <= $200 to the day. THEN THE DEFECT: the same phases data exists for all SEVEN blocks G17-G23 and the search stopped at two. Extending the IDENTICAL test to all 70 scored days gives TWELVE numb seams, of which 5 land at <= $200 - a 42% rate against a 24% base rate, not 5-of-6. And the split is total: the five hits are ALL in G20 and G23, while the six seams in G17, G18 and G19 are 0-FOR-6, with next-day |net| of 380, 420, 1230, 720, 360 and 420 (median 420). The effect is exactly co-extensive with the blocks that were searched. THE RANGE COROLLARY ALSO FAILS TO EXTEND: over all 12 seams the next-day median range is 1,205 against 1,140 for every other day - no compression at all, where the record measured 875 against 1,350. That happens to STRENGTHEN the corollary as worded ('a NET suppressor, NOT a volatility suppressor') while cutting the primary claim from 6.5x to 1.4x (median |net| 370 against 530).
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: WITHIN G20+G23, YES - the counterexample was named and kept, and 5/6 could have been 2/6. ACROSS THE CORPUS, NO: a search restricted to the two blocks where the mechanism was noticed cannot come out against it. That is the precise thing this audit exists to catch, and it is more dangerous here than in the sloppier plays because the record wears every mark of rigour - a declared D24 state, a named base rate, a kept counterexample, a self-declared boundary weakness. THE HONEST READ IS NOT THAT THE PLAY IS WRONG: 42% against a 24% base rate is still a real lift, and the mechanism is sound. The read is that its stated strength is 5-of-6 when its measured strength at full scope is 5-of-12, and the difference is a block boundary nobody drew on purpose.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES, and it is well-formed - 12 of 70 scored days fire (17%), which is a proper tail condition rather than a saturated one, and the k3 distribution is wide (p25 0.063, median 0.198, p75 0.367) so the 0.05 bar sits in the lower tail rather than at a cliff. Per block: g17 2/10, g18 3/10, g19 1/10, g20 3/10, g21 0/10, g22 0/10, g23 3/10 - degenerate (zero fires) in 2 of 7 blocks, which is normal for a tail. The condition is not the problem here; the corpus search behind it is.
audits.falsifier: STATED IN THE RECORD and it is the right one: 'a numb prior terminal phase followed by a large next-day NET with no new driver; or the range compressing as much as the net.' My extension produces four more instances of the first clause that were never named (g18 0429 -> +1,230; g18 0506 -> +720; g17 0424 -> +420; g19 0520 -> -420), and the second clause is where the play SURVIVES - at full scope the range does not compress at all (1,205 vs 1,140), so it is a net rule and not a volatility rule, exactly as claimed. The falsifier was written well and then run at 2-of-7 scope.
